# Running SGE jobs
## Correction to the moved text below (2026-10-14)
The listing-form wait loop in the moved text has no deadline, so it never exits for a job stuck in `Eqw` or `hqw`.
Use this form:

```bash deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + H_RT_SECONDS + 3600 )); absent=0 while [ $absent -lt 3 ]; do [ $(date +%s) -ge $deadline ] && { echo "TIMEOUT: check qstat -u phitro (Eqw/hqw?)"; break; } qstat -u phitro 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^ *<jobid> " && absent=0 || absent=$((absent+1)) sleep 45 done ```
**Cores: request what the job uses (2026-10-31; replaces "Cores" under Job defaults).** SGE charges every reserved core.
Over 14 days our jobs reserved 9143 core-h and used 3242 (35%); the EC523 arrays held 4-8 slots and used 1.1-1.25.
So:
- 1 slot unless a command in the script runs K threads; then put `# cores: <that command>` on the `-pe` line (`#$ -pe omp 8 # cores: diamond --threads $NSLOTS`) and pass `$NSLOTS` to it.
- Never add slots to get memory:
SCC enforces memory loosely (owner, 2026-10-31).
- Before choosing K for a job that ran before:
`tools/sge_efficiency.py lookup <name>` (config repo) shows its measured cores used.
After every job, with the artifact check:
`tools/sge_efficiency.py job <id>`;
OVER-RESERVED means lower K next time, and `qalter -pe omp <k> <id>` fixes array tasks still queued.
- Hook `qsub_guard` enforces this on qsub/qrsh/qalter:
K > 1 without a `# cores:` note is denied; a note contradicted by >= 2 measured runs is denied once.
A subagent's qsub is denied (rule 5).
**Host filters (2026-10-21, `qconf -sc`).** `-l mem_per_core=N` (relop `<=`) keeps only hosts with at least N per core;
12G matched only the 24G/core GPU nodes and job 8132228 sat 70 min in qw: keep mem_per_core at 8G or less.
A job in qw over 10 min: read the scheduling info in `qstat -j <id>`.
CPU test and eval jobs whose wheels need AVX2 (FBGEMM, torch CPU) request `-l avx2`: job 8171407 on a non-AVX2 host gave 6 false failures.
Claude runs inside an SGE job on a compute node (`$JOB_ID` set); the login-node limits below apply to work started from a login shell.
**Full test suite for a PR (2026-11-01):** run it through `tools/scc_ci_status.py submit`, which posts the `scc-tests` status on the commit.
